headline: High-risk shared-repo and autonomous-write pairing: Aider and Devin can conflict on the same codebase, with Devin also able to propagate Aider output into external systems.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aider reads and writes git-tracked files in a shared repo, and Devin can also read/write repo clones plus use MCP and browser-based workflows. That creates a plausible file-content injection path if one agent consumes the other's edited files as instructions. The profiles do not show a direct shared clipboard or message channel, so this is not high.
conditions: IF Devin ingests Aider-authored files as instructions without provenance checks
IF both agents operate on the same repository checkout or synchronized clone
mitigations: Add a short provenance banner to agent-generated files before handoff
Require manual review of any file containing imperative text before execution
Separate worktrees per agent for the same repo
Disable automatic instruction-following from repo content
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging in the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: Aider touches source code and git history in a shared git repo, while Devin touches source code, issue trackers, team chat, and docs and can write to GitHub, Slack, Jira, Linear, and Notion. If sensitive code or secrets land in the shared repo, Devin can move that data into broader collaboration surfaces by default. The profiles do not prove uncontrolled third-party exfiltration of secrets, so medium fits.
conditions: IF sensitive source code or secrets are present in the shared repository
IF Devin is permitted to post repo-derived content into Slack, Jira, Linear, or Notion
mitigations: Restrict Devin's write scopes to the minimum needed
Keep secrets out of the shared repo and use env vars or secret managers
Use a scrubber before any chat or ticket export
Review outbound messages for code or secret snippets
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on integration writes

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have unrestricted filesystem write, shell execution, network egress, and git-state modification. Aider explicitly shares state via a shared git repo, while Devin supports parallel sessions and shared integrations, so concurrent edits can collide and overwrite each other. Because the overlap is on the same mutable codebase and git state, the blast radius can include irreversible repository history damage.
conditions: IF both agents modify the same branch or working tree concurrently
IF git operations are performed without external locking or merge coordination
mitigations: Assign one agent per branch
Pause one agent while the other commits
Use a lockfile around git writes
Require pull/rebase before each commit
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency locks

D_cascading_error.rationale: Aider produces code edits and commits, and Devin can autonomously act in a cloud workspace with browser, shell, and write access to external systems. If Devin treats Aider's output as authoritative, a mistaken patch can cascade into commits, tickets, or chat updates without a verification step. That interaction is documented by the profiles' shared repo and autonomous execution model, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF Devin uses Aider-generated diffs or summaries as the basis for downstream actions
IF no human or automated verification step checks Aider's output before Devin acts
mitigations: Require a second-pass review before any downstream action
Limit Devin to read-only analysis on Aider outputs
Attach test results to every handoff
Block ticket or chat writes until diff review passes
requires-engineering: add verification gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Aider handles source code and git history locally as a user-run tool, while Devin is vendor-managed in a cloud workspace and also touches issue trackers, team chat, and docs. That creates a residency and retention mismatch for the same code-related data class, especially if code or metadata is copied into cloud integrations. The profiles do not show a specific regulated-data class like PHI, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF the same code or metadata is subject to a local-only handling policy
IF Devin stores or forwards that material into cloud integrations or vendor-managed storage
mitigations: Keep regulated or sensitive repos out of Devin's workspace
Use separate retention policies for chat and repo artifacts
Document which data classes may enter cloud tools
Review integration logs for residency-sensitive content
requires-engineering: align retention and residency controls across tools
